must_cover.point: Embeddings are numerical representations of real-world objects like words, sentences, or images converted into sequences of numbers called vectors.
They matter because computers and machine learning models cannot understand raw text or images directly; they need numbers to perform math and logic.
Unlike traditional codes that treat every item as completely unrelated, embeddings capture semantic meaning so that similar concepts are placed closer together in a multi-dimensional space.
Step 1: Raw data such as words or documents are fed into a trained neural network model.
Step 2: The model analyzes the contexts in which words or items appear across vast amounts of training data.
Step 3: The model outputs a dense vector, which is a list of numbers representing coordinates in a high-dimensional space.
Limitations include lossy compression where some fine details or exact nuances of the original text can be lost during vector creation.
A realistic use case is building a semantic search engine or recommendation system that finds documents or products with similar meanings rather than exact keyword matches.

facts: Embeddings map complex data into continuous vector spaces.
Common embedding vectors often have hundreds or thousands of dimensions, such as 768 or 1536 numbers.
Distance metrics like cosine similarity are used to measure how close or related two embedding vectors are.
Vector arithmetic can sometimes capture analogical relationships, such as king minus man plus woman equaling queen.
Machine learning models use embeddings to process text, images, audio, and categorical variables efficiently.

misconceptions.wrong: Embeddings are just encrypted versions of text or secret codes.
misconceptions.right: Embeddings are numerical coordinates that represent the semantic meaning and relationships of data.

misconceptions.wrong: Every word or object has only one fixed universal embedding vector for all time.
misconceptions.right: An embedding depends entirely on the specific machine learning model and training data used to generate it.

misconceptions.wrong: Embeddings contain exact dictionary definitions of words.
misconceptions.right: Embeddings capture contextual usage patterns and associations, not formal dictionary definitions.

misconceptions.wrong: Computers understand embeddings the exact same way humans understand language.
misconceptions.right: Computers only compute geometric distances and mathematical relationships between numbers.

misconceptions.wrong: Embeddings are only used for text processing.
misconceptions.right: Embeddings can represent images, audio, user profiles, and other complex real-world data types.
